targetAudience.primary: Architects and operators of long-running, effect-capable agent systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands checkpoints, retries, idempotency, and external APIs.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A restored agent can look locally correct while unknowingly duplicating or contradicting an effect that already escaped to an external system.

whyNow: New primary research reports substantial gains from aligned context-and-workspace rewind while explicitly bounding restoration to controlled state, exposing the missing external-effect contract.

externalHook.description: A worker returns to the moment before a remote call, but the remote service still contains the call's result.

coreProposition: Aligned checkpoint restoration can recover local causal consistency, but safe end-to-end recovery requires a separate, authoritative reconciliation of every external effect before retry, compensation, acceptance, or stop.

originalValue.description: Separates trajectory restoration, controlled-state restoration, and external-effect reconciliation, then derives an effect-ledger and resume-gate model from the demonstrated boundary.

readerTakeaway: Treat rewind as eligibility to reason again, not permission to replay; bind each escaped effect to an occurrence identity, checkpoint generation, authoritative target reread, and explicit recovery decision.

supported: AgentRewind restores model context and controlled workspace state at the same checkpoint and starts a new suffix with failure-derived memory.
The reported GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4 mini comparisons improve task success and checklist progress inside the evaluated harnesses.
The controlled rewind boundary is principally the workspace directory tree and does not automatically reverse remote effects.
A local rewind can therefore coexist with an already-materialized external effect.
unsupported: Automatic authorization to retry or compensate after rewind
uncertain: Minimum occurrence identity for ambiguous responses
Correct compensation protocol across heterogeneous systems
Concurrency semantics for overlapping recovered workers

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from public primary research and general external-effect semantics and remains independently useful.

decisionReason: The Research Object supports a concrete, bounded recovery architecture without enlarging local benchmark results into a global rollback claim.
